notes: In כִּי שָׁם בֵּיתוֹ the locative adverb is the predicate of the verbless clause, so the supplied was joins שָׁם rather than the noun (rule 20's adverbial anchor).

הָרָמָתָה is the directional predicate of the opening verbless clause, so the construction-supplied copula joins the directive he's unit and heads on the word written for the direction (rules 32, 49), while the article on the toponym is unrepresented.
